summary: Model tested: a long-range attraction among χ only, U = −G̃ m² W(|v−v′|/v*)/r, with ε ≡ G̃/G. The Hubble flow does close the gate between comoving χ pairs farther apart than r_gate = v*/H. For v* = 120 km/s that is 0.084 Mpc comoving at recombination, 1.56 Mpc at z = 3, a peak of 2.03 Mpc at z = 0.63, and 1.78 Mpc today. This does not hide the force from cosmology. In velocity units the gate closes at a Hubble-velocity separation of exactly v* at every epoch, and the Lyman-α forest measures power in those units: its pivot sits at k_p·v* = 1.08 for v* = 120 km/s. Linearizing the gated force about the Hubble flow gives two terms: the usual density term, cut off below k·s_c ≈ 1, and an anti-drag on χ peculiar velocities with rate (ε/2)Ω_c H. A brute-force quadrature confirms the anti-drag to 1e-5. The background expansion is unchanged at O(ε). Against the DESI DR1 compressed Lyman-α parameters (Δ² = 0.379 ± 0.032, n = −2.309 ± 0.019), linear theory gives the following upper bounds on ε (Gaussian gate; the range runs from the total-matter to the gas growth ratio): 0.029–0.081 at v* = 120 km/s, 0.014–0.023 at 300 km/s, about 0.015–0.024 from 500 to 3000 km/s, 0.35–1.1 at 30 km/s, and 3.1 (matter ratio; gas ratio >10) at 10 km/s. The bound comes mainly from the slope n, because the force switches on near the pivot scale. Above about 1000 km/s a crude mapping of the Planck+BOSS ungated limit (β < 0.0048) is stronger: ε ≲ 0.014 at 1000 km/s and 0.007 at 3000 km/s. If the gate instead uses peculiar velocities only, the force is ungated in linear cosmology and limits near 0.005 apply. Satellite tests are much weaker. Sgr moves at 311 km/s through a host with σ ≈ 150 km/s, so the ~10% stream limit becomes ε < 1.5 at v* = 120 km/s; Fornax gives ε < 1.3–3.3. The Bullet Cluster collision at 2600 km/s closes the gate (mean gate factor 1.0e-4), so it tests nothing below v* of about 1000 km/s. Inside dwarfs the gate is open (mean factor ≥ 0.84 for σ ≤ 30 km/s), so the force acts as extra dark-matter-only gravity; stars still measure the gravitational mass. The larger effect is earlier collapse: at the Lyman-α boundary for v* = 120 km/s, 10⁸ M☉ halos collapse at z = 3.72–4.36 instead of 3.40 (density proxy ×1.23–1.81), which makes dwarfs denser, the opposite of cores. Pairwise scattering by the long-range force is negligible: σ_T/m = 2.4e-62 cm²/g at 30 km/s for G̃ = G, scaling as G̃². Reaching 30 cm²/g would need G̃/G = 3.6e31, so the long-range force can neither supply the scattering benchmark nor affect row 2. Net result: for 30 ≲ v* ≲ 3000 km/s the gated force must be weaker than a few percent of gravity, ≲3–8% at the program's v* ≈ 120 km/s. ε ≈ 1 passes the compressed Lyman-α test only for v* ≲ 10–30 km/s, where small halos form much earlier; that regime was not bounded here.

claims.statement: Current bounds on an ungated dark-matter-only long-range force, with the force equal to β times gravity: (a) β < 0.011 (Planck) and β < 0.0054 (Planck+BAO) at 95% for mediator mass ≲ H0 ≈ 1e-33 eV (Archidiacono, Castorina, Redigolo, Salvioni 2022). (b) β < 0.012 (Planck) and β < 0.0048 (Planck + BOSS full shape + BAO) at 95% (Bottaro et al. 2024 PRL); BOSS DR12 is used to k_max = 0.20 (0.23) h/Mpc at z_eff = 0.32 (0.57), for ranges ≳ the size of the universe. (c) For ranges 100 kpc–10 Gpc (Bottaro et al. 2025): bounds strongest for m_φ/H0 = 10–10³; DESI BAO gives a mild 2σ preference for β ≈ 0.004 ± 0.002; no range-dependent numbers are given in the text. (d) Graham et al. 2025: earlier work excluded ranges ≳ 100 kpc with strength ≳ 1e-3–1e-2, while sub-Mpc forces orders of magnitude stronger than gravity remain allowed. Their Lyman-α criterion is a loose one, a growth factor ≳ 10 at recombination at k = 2/Mpc. (e) All of these are scalar-mediated models. Costa et al. 2025 report that their background effects (dark-matter mass change, scalar energy) suppress structure growth in CMB-compatible scenarios, so the bounds do not transfer one-to-one to the gated potential, which has no O(ε) background effect (K4).

claims.statement: Linear response of the gated force about the Hubble flow. Reading used: force = −∇ₓU at fixed velocities. The response has two terms. (i) A density term 4πG̃ρ̄_c R(k s_c) δ_c, with R(y) = y∫₀^∞ sin(yt)W(t)dt; for the Gaussian gate W = exp(−u²/2), R = √2·y·F(y/√2), F the Dawson function. (ii) An anti-drag on χ peculiar velocities, +(4π/3)(G̃ρ̄_c/H) R_v(k s_c) u, i.e. rate (ε/2)Ω_c(a)H at k s_c ≫ 1, where R_v(y) = 3∫₀¹μ²R(yμ)dμ for any W with W(0)=1 and W(∞)=0. Origin of the anti-drag: neighbours ahead of a moving particle recede from it more slowly than neighbours behind, so the gate is more open ahead. At k s_c ≫ 1 its strength depends on neither v* nor the gate shape. It raises the small-ε matter-era growth-exponent shift from 0.6ε to 0.8ε (single fluid). The homogeneous background is unchanged: a uniform medium exerts no net force. The background potential per particle, −(3/2)εΩ_c m v*² (Gaussian gate), is a fraction ~ε(v*/c)² = 1.6e-7 ε of m c² at v* = 120 km/s. So, unlike scalar-mediated forces (K1e), there is no O(ε) background effect. The Gaussian W reproduces the lab notebook's exp(−k²/μ²) with k = m v/2 and v* = √2 μ/m.
claims.basis: gate_kernels.py: closed forms checked against brute-force sine transforms. The anti-drag formula was checked by direct 2D quadrature of the force on a moving particle in a uniform Hubble-flow medium, for Gaussian and rational gates. misc_numbers.py: background integral and growth exponents.

claims.statement:
Literature on satellites and streams.
- Kesden & Kamionkowski 2006 (PRL 97, 131303): Sgr's near-equal streams challenge 'models in which DM and baryons accelerate differently by more than 10%'.
- Their PRD (74, 083007) uses a Yukawa force suppressed relative to gravity by β². The leading/trailing star ratio drops from 0.66 to 0.44, 0.091 and 0.0042 for forces of 1%, 4% and 9% of gravity (β = 0.1, 0.2, 0.3). Their exclusion statement is qualitative: 'a dark-matter force greater than 10% the strength of gravity is already excluded'.
- Kesden 2009 (PRD 80, 083530): a few percent gives O(1) changes; forces >10% are excluded; disputes simulations in which gravity-strength forces gave symmetric streams.
- Keselman, Nusser & Peebles 2010 (PRD 81, 063521; ReBEL, β = 1, comoving screening 1 Mpc/h): a preliminary hydro analysis found consistency with the McDonald et al. 2000 Lyman-α P1D at z ≈ 3, with free IGM parameters; this contrasts with K6.
- Zamlung & Nusser 2025 (Fornax, force (1+β)G): β ≳ 0.6 unbinds the bulk of the stars; β ≳ 0.4 excluded; β ≲ 0.2 broadly consistent.
- Bullet Cluster: the mass centroid moves at 2600 km/s, shock ~4700 km/s, consistent with ΛCDM (Springel & Farrar 2007). Farrar & Rosen 2007 had proposed a force 0.4–1.2× gravity.

claims.statement:
Satellite tests with the gate. The extra pull of a satellite's dark matter toward the host's dark matter is ε⟨W⟩·g_host, where ⟨W⟩ is the gate averaged over the relative-velocity distribution.
- Sgr: |V| = 311.1 km/s at 18.11 kpc. The host is an isothermal sphere matched to the Eilers et al. v_c = 212 km/s (σ_1D = 150 km/s); its orbit has pericentre 14.7 kpc and apocentre 46.8 kpc. ⟨W⟩ = 0.066 (Gaussian) / 0.21 (rational) at v* = 120. With the 10% limit this gives ε < 1.5 (Gaussian) / 0.48 (rational) at v* = 120; ε < 0.42 at 200, 0.22 at 300, 0.11 at 1000, and 0.10 at ≥ 2000 km/s.
- Fornax: |V| = 155.3 km/s at 149 kpc; pericentre 87.9 kpc at 253 km/s in the Zamlung–Nusser host. ⟨W⟩ = 0.12 at pericentre and 0.32 now (v* = 120). With β < 0.4 this gives ε < 3.3 (pericentre) or 1.3 (now); the limit tends to 0.40 at large v*.
Both are weaker than K6 at every v* ≥ 20 km/s and weaker than K9 above 300 km/s. Because the satellites move faster than v*, the gate suppresses these tests.

claims.statement: Dwarf halos. The mean internal gate for dark-matter pairs (pair dispersion √2σ) at v* = 120 km/s is 0.997 at σ = 3.7 km/s (Segue-1-like, †), 0.98 at 10 km/s (classical dSph, †), 0.84 at 30 km/s, 0.11 (rational 0.26) at 155 km/s (Milky Way) and 6e-4 at 1000 km/s (clusters). Satellites (ε ≳ 0.1–3) and the Bullet Cluster never dominate. Scattering is irrelevant. At the program's v* ≈ 120 km/s the gated χ-only force must be weaker than about 3–8% of gravity (Gaussian) or 2–5% (rational). ε = 1 passes the compressed Lyman-α test only for v* ≲ 10–30 km/s (Gaussian, spanning the matter–gas bracket) or v* ≲ 10 km/s (rational). There the linear collapse epoch of 10⁸ M☉ halos moves from z ≈ 3.4 to z ≈ 9–35 (K11), a regime constrained by small-scale probes that this run did not compute.

scripts: (each script's printed output is saved beside it as <name>.out; halo_formation_gasbounds.out holds the halo-formation run at the gas-ratio boundary, using the command-line points 0.081 120 0.42 50 0.17 80 0.037 200 1.14 30)
open_questions: A real Lyman-α likelihood: the DESI DR1 P1D (and high-resolution spectra at k ≳ 0.02 s/km) fitted with the gated linear power, with IGM marginalization and hydrodynamic simulations run with the force. The compressed-parameter bound of K6 is an estimate, and its O(1) factor is uncertain (matter vs gas ratio alone spans ×2.8 at v* = 120 km/s).

A bound for v* ≲ 20–30 km/s from small-scale structure: high-k P1D, the reionization optical depth, ultra-faint-dwarf heating (Graham & Ramani 2024 use k = 300/Mpc), Milky Way satellite counts and central densities. At the compressed Lyman-α boundary the collapse epoch of 10⁸ M☉ halos moves to z ≈ 9–35, and nothing computed here tests that.

How to read a velocity-dependent potential. This run uses force = −∇ₓU at fixed velocities. A Lagrangian reading adds d/dt(∂U/∂v) terms of the same O(ε) order (a renormalized peculiar momentum), which would change the O(1) coefficients of K4–K6.

A covariant definition of the relative velocity between separated particles. Parallel transport along the constant-time slice gives the Hubble-flow gate used here; a peculiar-velocity gate gives the ungated case (K10). The program defines neither.

Whether any program mechanism yields a long-range gated force. In the record, X is massive (range < 37.7 μm in the aligned vacuum, phase-space-diameter note §8.2) and the gate acts at contact range through fiber overlap (gate-mechanism page). A long-range gated force would need a massless carrier that the record does not contain. This is a question for the program-side analysis.
Nonlinear dynamics inside halos with σ ~ v*, where the attraction selects co-moving pairs (the velocity-clumping question itself), was outside this task.

Linear theory throughout. Nonlinear IGM evolution under the force is not modeled; Keselman, Nusser & Peebles found qualitative IGM changes (emptier voids). Their preliminary 2010 analysis found a gravity-strength ReBEL force with 1 Mpc/h comoving screening consistent with the 2000-era P1D when IGM parameters floated. That contrasts with K6, where ε = 1 at v* = 120 km/s shifts the pivot slope by +1.3.

The compressed parameters assume a ΛCDM-like shape near k_p. The gated force puts a slope feature at the pivot, and the bound is driven by that slope, so the bound depends on the compression capturing such a feature.

The eps = 0 baseline is Rogers & Poulin's Planck+BAO+SNe prediction from a Σmν-extension chain, not pure ΛCDM. The EH98 no-wiggle transfer function is from memory (†); it matches that published prediction to 3.6% in Δ² and 0.002 in n.

Reductions in the growth model: baryons are held unclustered before z_drag and pressureless after; radiation is smooth (Meszaros); the massive neutrino is smooth; the gas ratio is the baryon growth ratio. The pair-velocity smoothing uses a constant-s1 Gaussian average, and it is formally second order.
The BOSS mapping (K9) matches one (k, z) of linear power excess. The published bounds come from full likelihoods of scalar-mediated models whose background effects are absent in the gated model.

Satellite translations assume an isotropic, position-independent Maxwellian host velocity distribution and the mapping β → ε⟨W⟩. The Kesden–Kamionkowski 10% limit is qualitative and was disputed by gravity-strength simulations (Kesden 2009 rebuts them). Fornax uses the reconstructed Zamlung–Nusser host, which overpredicts v_c at 18 kpc, so Sgr uses an isothermal host matched to Eilers et al.
Bullet Cluster dispersions come from search summaries: Barrena et al. 2002 via a secondary source, plus DS+ 2022.

Values from memory (†), not checked: Segue 1 σ = 3.7 km/s; classical dSph σ ≈ 10 km/s; satellite internal dispersion 12 km/s; R0 = 8.122 kpc; growth-index anchor Ω_m^0.55; EH98 formula coefficients. The photon density was checked from a_rad T⁴ (2.473e-5 h⁻²). Physical constants are CODATA [T].
The χ thermal-velocity numbers (K3) are an illustration under an assumed dark-sector temperature, which P4-strict leaves unspecified.
Collapse redshifts from σ(M) = 1.686 and the (1+z_c)³ density scaling are proxies, not halo-structure predictions.
Anti-drag and density kernels assume a smooth W (analytic in the vector relative velocity). A gate with a cusp at zero relative velocity was not treated.
